item.title: AggregatedInputOutputStatusBody
item.description:
Status information for the Source or Destination, aggregated across all Worker Processes.

Fields#

Field Type Required Description
health Literal["Green", "Red", "Unknown", "Yellow"] Yes Overall health status of the Source or Destination.
healthCounts HealthCountType Yes Counts of health statuses for the Source or Destination across all Worker Processes. Includes only statuses with non-zero counts.
timestamp int Yes Timestamp (in Unix time) when the status was last updated.
error StatusError | None No Error information, if applicable.
metrics dict[str, Any] | None No Metrics data for the Source or Destination, including base metrics, aggregated across all Worker Processes. For load-balanced Destinations, includes item-level metrics.
pq AggregatedPQStatus | None No Persistent queue status information (if persistent queue is enabled).

Example#

from cribl_python_sdk import AggregatedInputOutputStatusBody

obj = AggregatedInputOutputStatusBody(
 health="Green",
 healthCounts={},
 timestamp=0,
)

timestamp int Yes Timestamp (in Unix time) when the persistent queue status was last updated.
error StatusError | None No Error information for the persistent queue, if applicable.

Example#

from cribl_python_sdk import AggregatedPQStatus

item.title: ApiCredentialCreateResponseSchema
item.description:
API Credential returned when created. Includes the Client Secret.

Fields#

Field Type Required Description
name str Yes Human-readable name of the API Credential.
description str Yes Brief description of the purpose and usage for the API Credential.
enabled bool Yes If true, the API Credential is enabled. Otherwise, false.
organizationId str Yes Unique ID of the Organization.
clientId str Yes Client ID for the API Credential.
roles ApiCredentialRolesSchema Yes Role assignments for the API Credential.
ipAllowlist list[str] Yes CIDR range enforced as the IP allowlist for the API Credential. An empty array means that the API Credential has no IP restrictions.
createdBy str Yes Member who created the API Credential.
createdDate str Yes ISO 8601 timestamp when the API Credential was created.
lastUpdatedBy str Yes Member who last updated the API Credential.
lastUpdatedDate str Yes ISO 8601 timestamp when the API Credential was last updated.
clientSecret str Yes Client Secret for the API Credential. The Client Secret is sensitive information and should be kept private. Returned only in the POST response when the API Credential is created. Never returned in GET responses. If you need the Client Secret again, you must rotate credentials and retrieve the new Client Secret from the POST response.

Used by#

  • client.cloud.api_credentials.create()

Example#

from cribl_python_sdk.models import ApiCredentialCreateResponseSchema

obj = ApiCredentialCreateResponseSchema(
 name="example",
 description="example",
 enabled=True,
 organizationId="example",
 clientId="example",
 roles={"organizationRole": "owner"},
 ipAllowlist=["example"],
 createdBy="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
 createdDate="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
 lastUpdatedBy="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
 lastUpdatedDate="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
 clientSecret="example",
)

appBackendMaxCallbacksTotal int No Maximum number of broker callbacks per minute across all app backend installations on this Leader. Unlimited when unset. Over-limit callbacks receive HTTP 429.

item.title: AuthType
item.description:
Credentials to use when authenticating with the schema registry

Fields#

Field Type Required Description
disabled bool Yes Disabled
oauthEnabled bool | None No Authenticate with the schema registry using OAuth instead of basic HTTP authentication
tokenUrl str | None No URL of the token endpoint to use for OAuth authentication
clientId str | None No Client ID to use for OAuth authentication
oauthSecretType str | None No Source of the OAuth client secret.
clientTextSecret str | None No Select or create a stored text secret
oauthParams list[OauthParamConfInputKafka] | None No Additional fields to send to the token endpoint, such as scope or audience
identityPoolId str | None No Confluent Cloud identity pool ID. Sent as the Confluent-Identity-Pool-Id header on requests to the schema registry.
logicalCluster str | None No Confluent Cloud Schema Registry logical cluster ID. Sent as the target-sr-cluster header on requests to the schema registry.
credentialsSecret str | None No Select or create a secret that references your credentials
xtemplate_tokenUrl str | None No Binds ’tokenUrl’ to a variable for dynamic value resolution. Set to variable ID (pack-scoped) or ‘cribl.’/’edge.’ prefixed ID (group-scoped). Variable value overrides ’tokenUrl’ at runtime.
xtemplate_clientId str | None No Binds ‘clientId’ to a variable for dynamic value resolution. Set to variable ID (pack-scoped) or ‘cribl.’/’edge.’ prefixed ID (group-scoped). Variable value overrides ‘clientId’ at runtime.
xtemplate_identityPoolId str | None No Binds ‘identityPoolId’ to a variable for dynamic value resolution. Set to variable ID (pack-scoped) or ‘cribl.’/’edge.’ prefixed ID (group-scoped). Variable value overrides ‘identityPoolId’ at runtime.
xtemplate_logicalCluster str | None No Binds ’logicalCluster’ to a variable for dynamic value resolution. Set to variable ID (pack-scoped) or ‘cribl.’/’edge.’ prefixed ID (group-scoped). Variable value overrides ’logicalCluster’ at runtime.

Example#

from cribl_python_sdk.models.nested import AuthType

obj = AuthType(
 disabled=True,
)

initialBackoff float | None No Initial value used to calculate the retry, in milliseconds. Maximum is 600,000 ms (10 minutes).
backoffRate float | None No Set the backoff multiplier (2-20) to control the retry frequency for failed messages. For faster retries, use a lower multiplier. For slower retries with more delay between attempts, use a higher multiplier. The multiplier is used in an exponential backoff formula; see the Kafka documentation for details.
authenticationTimeout float | None No Maximum time to wait for Kafka to respond to an authentication request
reauthenticationThreshold float | None No Specifies a time window during which @{product} can reauthenticate if needed. Creates the window measuring backward from the moment when credentials are set to expire.

If the client sends no heartbeats to the broker before the timeout expires, the broker will remove the client from the group and initiate a rebalance. Value must be between the broker’s configured group.min.session.timeout.ms and group.max.session.timeout.ms. See Kafka’s documentation for details.

heartbeatInterval float | None No Expected time between heartbeats to the consumer coordinator when using Kafka’s group-management facilities. Value must be lower than sessionTimeout and typically should not exceed 1/3 of the sessionTimeout value. See Kafka’s documentation for details.
autoCommitInterval float | None No How often to commit offsets. If both this and Offset commit threshold are set, @{product} commits offsets when either condition is met. If both are empty, @{product} commits offsets after each batch.
autoCommitThreshold float | None No How many events are needed to trigger an offset commit. If both this and Offset commit interval are set, @{product} commits offsets when either condition is met. If both are empty, @{product} commits offsets after each batch.

timeoutRetrySettings TimeoutRetrySettingsType | None No Retry settings for HTTP requests that exceed the request timeout.

OutputKafka — a Destination variant.

Fields#

Field Type Required Description
type Literal["kafka"] No
id str | None No Unique name for this output
pipeline str | None No Pipeline to process data before sending out to this output
systemFields list[str] | None No Fields to automatically add to events, such as cribl_pipe. Supports wildcards.
environment str | None No Optionally, enable this config only on a specified Git branch. If empty, will be enabled everywhere.
streamtags list[str] | None No Metadata tags used for categorization and filtering.
brokers list[str] Yes Enter each Kafka bootstrap server you want to use. Specify hostname and port, e.g., mykafkabroker:9092, or just hostname, in which case @{product} will assign port 9092.
topic str Yes The topic to publish events to. Can be overridden using the __topicOut field.
ack int | None No Control the number of required acknowledgments.
format Literal["json", "raw", "protobuf"] | None No Format to use to serialize events before writing to Kafka.
compression Literal["none", "gzip", "snappy", "lz4", "zstd"] | None No Codec to use to compress the data before sending to Kafka
maxRecordSizeKB float | None No Maximum size of each record batch before compression. The value must not exceed the Kafka brokers’ message.max.bytes setting.
flushEventCount float | None No The maximum number of events you want the Destination to allow in a batch before forcing a flush
flushPeriodSec float | None No The maximum amount of time you want the Destination to wait before forcing a flush. Shorter intervals tend to result in smaller batches being sent.
kafkaSchemaRegistry KafkaSchemaRegistryAuthenticationTypeTemplateschemaRegistryUrlAuth | None No Kafka Schema Registry Authentication
connectionTimeout float | None No Maximum time to wait for a connection to complete successfully
requestTimeout float | None No Maximum time to wait for Kafka to respond to a request
maxRetries float | None No If messages are failing, you can set the maximum number of retries as high as 100 to prevent loss of data
maxBackOff float | None No The maximum wait time for a retry, in milliseconds. Default (and minimum) is 30,000 ms (30 seconds); maximum is 180,000 ms (180 seconds).
initialBackoff float | None No Initial value used to calculate the retry, in milliseconds. Maximum is 600,000 ms (10 minutes).
backoffRate float | None No Set the backoff multiplier (2-20) to control the retry frequency for failed messages. For faster retries, use a lower multiplier. For slower retries with more delay between attempts, use a higher multiplier. The multiplier is used in an exponential backoff formula; see the Kafka documentation for details.
authenticationTimeout float | None No Maximum time to wait for Kafka to respond to an authentication request
reauthenticationThreshold float | None No Specifies a time window during which @{product} can reauthenticate if needed. Creates the window measuring backward from the moment when credentials are set to expire.
sasl SaslAuthentication | None No Authentication parameters to use when connecting to brokers. Using TLS is highly recommended.
tls TlsSettingsClient | None No TLS settings (client side)
onBackpressure Literal["block", "drop", "queue"] | None No How to handle events when all receivers are exerting backpressure
description str | None No Optional description for this configuration.
protobufLibraryId str | None No Select a set of Protobuf definitions for the events you want to send
protobufEncodingId str | None No Select the type of object you want the Protobuf definitions to use for event encoding
pqStrictOrdering bool | None No Use FIFO (first in, first out) processing. Disable to forward new events to receivers before queue is flushed.
pqRatePerSec float | None No Throttling rate (in events per second) to impose while writing to Destinations from PQ. Defaults to 0, which disables throttling.
pqMode Literal["error", "always", "backpressure"] | None No In Error mode, PQ writes events to the filesystem if the Destination is unavailable. In Backpressure mode, PQ writes events to the filesystem when it detects backpressure from the Destination. In Always On mode, PQ always writes events to the filesystem.
pqMaxBufferSize float | None No Maximum number of events to hold in memory before writing the events to disk. Deprecated and only supported in workers < v4.17.0. Use pqMaxBufferSizeBytes instead.
pqMaxBackpressureSec float | None No How long (in seconds) to wait for backpressure to resolve before engaging the queue
pqMaxFileSize str | None No The maximum size to store in each queue file before closing and optionally compressing (KB, MB, etc.)
pqMaxSize str | None No The maximum disk space that the queue can consume (as an average per Worker Process) before queueing stops. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc.
pqPath str | None No The location for the persistent queue files. To this field’s value, the system will append: //.
pqCompress Literal["none", "gzip"] | None No Codec to use to compress the persisted data
pqOnBackpressure Literal["block", "drop"] | None No How to handle events when the queue is exerting backpressure (full capacity or low disk). ‘Block’ is the same behavior as non-PQ blocking. ‘Drop new data’ throws away incoming data, while leaving the contents of the PQ unchanged.
pqMaxBufferSizeBytes str | None No The maximum size to hold in memory before writing events to disk. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc. The minimum value is 64KB and the maximum value is 10MB.
pqControls dict[str, Any] | None No Persistent queue controls.
xtemplate_streamtags str | None No Binds ‘streamtags’ to a variable for dynamic value resolution. Set to variable ID (pack-scoped) or ‘cribl.’/’edge.’ prefixed ID (group-scoped). Variable value overrides ‘streamtags’ at runtime.
xtemplate_topic str | None No Binds ’topic’ to a variable for dynamic value resolution. Set to variable ID (pack-scoped) or ‘cribl.’/’edge.’ prefixed ID (group-scoped). Variable value overrides ’topic’ at runtime.
xtemplate_format str | None No Binds ‘format’ to a variable for dynamic value resolution. Set to variable ID (pack-scoped) or ‘cribl.’/’edge.’ prefixed ID (group-scoped). Variable value overrides ‘format’ at runtime.
xtemplate_compression str | None No Binds ‘compression’ to a variable for dynamic value resolution. Set to variable ID (pack-scoped) or ‘cribl.’/’edge.’ prefixed ID (group-scoped). Variable value overrides ‘compression’ at runtime.
xtemplate_onBackpressure str | None No Binds ‘onBackpressure’ to a variable for dynamic value resolution. Set to variable ID (pack-scoped) or ‘cribl.’/’edge.’ prefixed ID (group-scoped). Variable value overrides ‘onBackpressure’ at runtime.

Used by#

  • client.destinations.create()
  • client.destinations.update()

Example#

from cribl_python_sdk.models.outputs import OutputKafka

obj = OutputKafka(
 brokers=["example"],
 topic="example",
)

item.title: PqType
item.description:
Persistent queue settings for this Source.

Fields#

Field Type Required Description
mode Literal["smart", "always"] | None No With Smart mode (deprecated), PQ will write events to the filesystem only when it detects backpressure from the processing engine. Smart mode will have no new development starting July 2026, followed by End of Support and feature removal (auto-migrating to Always On) in January 2027. We recommend using Always On mode instead. With Always On mode, PQ will always write events directly to the queue before forwarding them to the processing engine.
maxBufferSizeBytes str | None No The maximum size to hold in memory before writing events to disk. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc. The minimum value is 64KB and the maximum value is 10MB.
maxBufferSize float | None No Maximum number of events to hold in memory before writing the events to disk. Deprecated and only supported in workers < v4.17.0. Use maxBufferSizeBytes instead.
commitFrequency float | None No The number of events to send downstream before committing that Stream has read them. Lower values increase cursor-write IOPS and can add disk pressure, including on shared storage.
maxFileSize str | None No The maximum size to store in each queue file before closing and optionally compressing. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc.
maxSize str | None No The maximum disk space that the queue can consume (as an average per Worker Process) before queueing stops. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc.
path str | None No The location for the persistent queue files. To this field’s value, the system will append: //inputs/
